VIRGINIA NAREDO naredonoi@gmail.com Dear Ms. Naredo: This has reference to the email dated 28 February 2024 requesting for clarification on whether a barangay may validly impose fees pertaining to the issuance of a Certificate to File Action (CFA). You maintain that Barangay Mayapa has collected a fee of Php 150.00 for the issuance of CFA where an official receipt will be issued as part of the barangay's miscellaneous fee. Local government units (LGUs) are statutorily endowed with the power to create sources of revenue pursuant to Sec. 1291 of RA 7160, subject to the fundamental principles and common limitations provided under Secs. 1302 and 1333 of the Code. Further, Sections 329-334 (Barangay Budget) of the Local Government Code of RA No. 7160 provide the basis for the collection, safekeeping and use of barangay funds. SECTION 129. Power to Create Source of Revenue - Each local govemment unit shall exercise its power to create its own sources revenue and to levy taxes, fees, and charges subject to the provisions herein, consistent with the basic policy of local autonomy. Such taxes, fees, and charges shall accrue exclusively to the local government units. SECTION 130. Fundamental Principles. - The following fundamental principles shall govem the exercise of the taxing and other revenue-raising poær-s of local govemment units: (1) (2) (3) (4) Taxation shall be uniform in each læal government unit; Taxes, fees, charges and other impositions shall: (a) (b) (c) (d) be equitable and based as far as practicable on the taxpayer's ability to pay; be levied and collected only for public purposes; not be adjust, excessive, oppressive, or confiscatory; not be contrary to law, public policy, national econonnic policy, or in restraint of trade; The collection of local taxes, fees, charges and other impositions shall in no case be let to any private person; The revenue collected pursuant to the provisions of this Code shall inure solely to the benefit of, and be subject to disposition by, the local govemment unit levying the tax, fee, charge or other imposition unless otherwise specifically provided herein; and, 60 (5) Each local govemment unit shall, as far as practicable, evolve a progressive system of taxation. SECTION 133. Common Limitations on the Taxing Powers Of Local Govemment Units. - Unless otherwise provided herein, the exercise of the taxing power-s of provinces, cities, municipalities, and Barangays shall not extend to the levy of the following: 65 (32) Income tax, except when levied on banks and other financial institutions; The aforesaid provisions govem the preparation, effectivity, and review of the barangay budget, including the financial procedures that the barangay shall observe. It bears to emphasize that under Sec. 152 par (d)4 of the same law, there is no express mention that the barangay may levy reasonable fees and charges in relation to the processing of a case yet to be filed in court. In fact, the express provision of the law only limits the imposition of fees and charges to the following: (1) On commercial breeding of fighting cocks, cockfighting an cockpits; (2) On places of recreation which charge admission fees; and (3) On billboards, signboards, neon signs, and outdoor advertisements. On the other hand, the Katarungang Pambarangay Law provides that a filing fee may be imposed by the 'upon members standing as mediators of the conciliation body. In case the party is unable to pay the filing fees due to inadequate financial means, he may file the case as an indigent by complying with the requirements set forth under par(f) of A. M. No. 08-8-7-SC 5. In case of an indigent party, payment of additional fees is avoided in order to afford the litigant the right to his day in Court. Under the aforecited law, payment for the issuance of a Certificate to File Action was not mentioned. Premises considered, we opine that a barangay may not levy and validly impose fees for the issuance of a Certificate to File Action. We thank you for bringing the matter before our Office. Rest assured that we will be closely monitoring the matter. Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AU HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN TOR R.
